{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZfgWww", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDGryY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 97, "title": "Add opt-in incoming Internet mail and browser-local external replies", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `835869debf834926121c949d5106acdedd188faf`, users can save outgoing Internet letters but cannot receive or reply to an Internet correspondent in PC-VAN mail.

`src/storage/schema.ts` requires a local `senderId`; its external-address branch permits outgoing human letters only. `createHumanMail` explicitly rejects Internet reply parents. `src/commands.ts` routes REPLY through the sender's member ID, and `src/mail.ts` assumes incoming senders are members. Consequently, the incoming-letter → INBOX → READ → REPLY journey is unavailable.

This is an existing fidelity gap. Completed outbound-mail Issue #93 and TELNET Issue #95 explicitly deferred incoming PC-VAN Internet mail.

## Expected outcome

An existing selected human can explicitly add one original fictional Internet letter through modern Settings, then complete:

`Settings sample action → ordinary mail entry → INBOX → READ → REPLY → compose/review/EDIT → explicit browser-local save → SENT/READ → reload and JSON backup/restore`

Use one fictional correspondent such as `observer@letters.example.invalid` and a short original Japanese letter consistent with everyday late-1996 interests. Preserve its address independently of members. Clearly identify sample loading as a local demonstration and outgoing replies as local saves with no transmission.

Loading remains opt-in and idempotent per recipient. Startup, registration, reload, reset and restoration must not automatically add this sample. Retain the existing shared mailbox projection through MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and SIG `MAIL`, including distinct entry and return contexts.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction judgment

Sources researched live on 2026-10-24:

- [Internet Magazine, November 1996, printed page 221](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf) lists both sending and receiving limits for PC-VAN Internet mail and specifies `INET#` destinations. Its sending-only qualification concerns automatic binary conversion. Confidence is high for text-mail reception and addressing; it supplies no complete incoming-header or reply sequence. PDF text was inspected; page-image retrieval failed.
- [Internet Magazine, October 1994, printed pages 106–107](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199410-104-bbs.pdf) distinguishes Internet addresses from intra-service IDs and documents PC-VAN's prefix. Confidence is high within 1994, with target-year addressing corroborated above. Its illustrated composer belongs to NIFTY-Serve.
- [Searchdesk's participant account dated May 1, 1999](https://searchdesk.com/help/history.html) recalls PC-VAN Internet mail and overseas mailing-list participation around 1994. This provides moderate-confidence cultural corroboration, without establishing typical usage or host controls.

Focused searches for incoming senders, replies and target-year mail controls recovered no qualifying complete PC-VAN session. Earlier [January 1994 gateway documentation](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/agrmet1943/49/4/49_4_297/_pdf) has badly damaged extraction and cannot prescribe 1996 routing. The [April 1995 comparison](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199504-104-bbs.pdf) places its gateway-sender/reply discussion under NIFTY-Serve; do not import those IDs or controls into PC-VAN. A [November 1996 mailing-list compilation](https://groups.google.com/g/fj.archives.answers/c/xQrZS1ki0Tk) resurfaced through snippets, but direct retrieval failed; no requirement depends on it.

Judgment: reception is sufficiently supported to implement this core journey. The sample-loading action, fictional correspondence, sender presentation, reply destination selection, editor behavior and local persistence are category D reconstruction. Exact gateway identity, header geometry and current/old/SIG mailbox relationships remain unresolved. Do not manufacture historical commands, gateway accounts or functioning addresses for synthetic members.

### Implementation boundaries and existing evidence

Inspect and extend the existing mail representation and transaction paths in `src/storage/schema.ts` and `src/storage/repository.ts`, composition/routing in `src/commands.ts`, rendering in `src/mail.ts`, and the Settings action/dialog patterns. Review affected mail indexes and consumers when allowing an incoming sender without a member ID. Reuse existing address validation, number allocation, read markers, calendar projection and literal-text composer.

`src/ai/mail.ts:pairMail` and its target checks restrict resident correspondence context. Preserve that boundary explicitly for both incoming external letters and outgoing replies. Do not introduce external members, resident personas, generated external replies or another identity registry.

Live repository searches returned no open Issues or PRs. [#93](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/93) and [#95](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/95) distinguish this scope from completed work. Inventory can change and lexical searches are incomplete.

[PR #96](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/96) matches the baseline merge. Its description and `docs/validation.md` report 340 passing checks, configured TypeScript checking/build and production TELNET journeys, with an initially incorrect assertion corrected. These are Coordinator records; this research graph ran no application, build, tests or inference.

Scope excludes real mail transport, arbitrary incoming-message editing, attachments, mailing-list subscriptions, delivery simulation, new AI activity, mailbox migration and changes to TELNET's separate bundled mailbox.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add a clearly labeled modern Settings action that targets the existing active human and explains that it adds one fictional letter locally. Without a human, explain how to register/select one without creating an identity automatically. Repeated activation, retries and concurrent tabs create no duplicate existing sample for that recipient. Another human can explicitly add their own copy. Restored-empty worlds remain empty until explicit activation.
- [ ] Represent incoming external identity separately from local member identity within the existing mail/backup architecture. Require a valid bounded address, an existing human recipient and explicit fictional-sample provenance. Reject contradictory identities, malformed addresses, unknown fields, missing/nonhuman recipients and forged resident simulation or recipient-confirmation fields. Retain existing text/control limits and backward compatibility with resident mail, outbound-only Internet records and backups lacking mail.
- [ ] INBOX/LIST and READ show the external sender address, selected human recipient, original subject/body, existing historical-date projection and human unread/read state. Do not substitute a synthetic member token or infer a resident identity. READ marks only that human's received letter read; other humans cannot select it through their mailbox. The sample indication must not imply actual network reception.
- [ ] REPLY to the received external letter pins its external destination and parent through review, EDIT and retry, using the existing `INET#` outgoing path. A reply parent must be an earlier incoming letter to the same human from the same external address. Reject missing, later, cross-human, different-correspondent and local/external-mismatched parents on writes and imports. Preserve ordinary outgoing Internet composition without a parent and all resident reply rules.
- [ ] Only explicit review approval saves the outgoing reply. SENT/READ retain its address and parent reference and truthfully report browser-local saving without external transmission or recipient-read evidence. Preserve literal Japanese, whitespace, blank lines, command-shaped text, cancellation, committed-draft consumption and retry after failure. Keep all three mail routes and their existing contextual returns working.
- [ ] Sample insertion and reply saving share existing atomic, monotonic numbering. Verify idempotent concurrent saves, conflicting-ID rejection and rollback on quota/transaction failure without a partial letter or consumed number. Reload and backup/restore preserve address, provenance, parent and read marker. Existing reset/restore and cross-tab invalidation prevent stale sample actions or reviewed drafts from mutating a replacement world.
- [ ] External correspondence never enters resident pair memory, generation targets, forum/OLT prompts or acquaintance calculations, and does not consume resident-mail activity limits. Loading/reading/replying creates no members, resident confirmations, public contributions, scheduling or model-consent changes. With activity paused, compare protected records while allowing the intended mail/read changes and existing session bookkeeping. Observe no external requests, address lookup, mailto handoff or model loading caused by the journey.
- [ ] Extend existing `tests/mail-repository.spec.ts`, `tests/mail.spec.ts`, `tests/mail-presentation.spec.ts` and relevant Settings coverage. Cover the production keyboard journey, all three entry routes, recipient isolation, strict import variants, legacy compatibility, concurrency/rollback, review/edit/cancellation, reload/JSON round-trip and reset/restore invalidation. Preserve private-context, resident-confirmation, simulated-IME and terminal pacing/skip coverage. Use deterministic fixtures or existing mocked inference.
- [ ] Update `docs/mail.md`, applicable storage documentation, historical research, README and Settings/About disclosures. Record source URLs, inspection dates, historical scope, confidence, failed retrievals and category D choices. Explain inclusion in backups/logs and keep PC-VAN incoming mail distinct from TELNET remote mail. Replace obsolete inbound-excluded descriptions only where this increment changes them.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test` before merge; existing Playwright configuration includes TypeScript checking and production bundling. Review the complete diff, documentation links and whitespace, and record actual results, failures and skipped checks. No new framework or real-model execution is required.

## Optional validation

Compare sender presentation and reply handling with a subsequently recovered dated PC-VAN incoming-mail session. Additional browser engines and native-IME checks are optional; human or hardware confirmation is not a completion gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks can be completed against local production assets before merge.
